articles.title: 史上最大 IPO 带来新一轮造富神话：Anthropic 上市或催生数千名百万富翁
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 19 日消息，据路透社今天（19 日）上午报道，随着 AI 初创企业 Anthropic 的上市，数千名现任和前员工有望凭借手中的公司股票成为百万美元富翁，就算这些财富暂时还停留在账面上也无妨。此次 IPO 有望成为硅谷历史上规模最大的员工造富事件之一。Anthropic 的员工有望迎来巨额财富增长，受益者不仅包括早期研究人员和工程师，还包括获得股权激励的行政人员。Anthropic 招股书披露了员工股权奖励的整体价值，却没有说明这些财富具体如何分配，因此外界对于员工能够获得多少财富，估算结果差异很大。旧金山非上市公司股权交易平台 Hill 预计，Anthropic 上市后，将有 598 名非创始人员工的持股价值分别达到至少 1 亿美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 6.68 亿元人民币）。Hill CEO 安德鲁 · 本森说：“很多人都希望自己持有的股权能够增值到足以改变人生的程度。没有比这更好的结果了。”本森认为，Anthropic 早期员工可能比临近上市时才加入的高管赚得更多：“那些最初只是基层员工的人，最终获得的财务回报，实际上应该比上市前才加入公司的高管更加丰厚。”私募市场研究机构 Sacra 则估计，如果按照发行价区间中间水平对应的 1.35 万亿美元（现汇率约合 9.02 万亿元人民币）估值计算，Anthropic 约 2800 名现任和前员工持有的已归属股权，税前价值可能分别超过 100 万美元（现汇率约合 668.1 万元人民币）。Sacra 研究主管马塞洛 · 巴尔韦指出，获得风险投资的公司向行政、支持和初级岗位员工授予股权并不少见。但以往随着企业规模扩大、工资待遇提高，许多公司会逐渐取消这些岗位的入职股权奖励，改为根据工作表现和任职年限发放。两家机构均强调，估算结果来自基于公开信息建立的模型，考虑了股权归属期、期权行权、股权要约交易、期权及限制性股票奖励、授予时间、员工人数和留任率等因素。路透社无法独立核实这些数字，Anthropic 的招股书也没有披露每名员工持有的股权价值。尽管如此，Anthropic 员工手中的潜在财富仍然十分惊人。公司披露，截至 9 月 30 日，员工等期权持有人的账面收益达到 1,190 亿美元（现汇率约合 7,950.13 亿元人民币），期权加权平均行权价仅为每股 2.91 美元（现汇率约合 19.4 元人民币）。其中约 730 亿美元（现汇率约合 4,876.97 亿元人民币）对应的期权满足了服务期归属条件，可以立即行权。五年前 Anthropic 刚刚成立时加入公司的员工，即使最初只担任行政或初级职位，也可能获得足以改变人生的财富，因为他们持有的一些股票期权，行权价甚至不到每股 1 美元（现汇率约合 6.7 元人民币）。招股书显示，在 2023 年及以前授予、截至 2023 年底仍未行权的股票期权，平均行权价只有 0.52 美元（现汇率约合 3.5 元人民币）。根据 Anthropic 的安排，非创始人员工可以在上市首个交易日出售最多 10% 的持股，待 2026 财年业绩公布后，还可以再出售最多 35%。Anthropic 成立于 2021 年，员工人数随着 AI 热潮迅速增加，从 2024 年底的约 940 人增至今年 9 月 30 日的约 5300 人。为吸引大量人才加入，公司广泛采用股权激励。Anthropic 在 2024 年 5 月发布的一则行政业务合作伙伴招聘信息显示，股权奖励并非 AI 研究人员和工程师的专属福利。该岗位负责管理公司高管日程、协调会议安排，以及处理费用申报和报销等事务，年薪为 14 万至 19 万美元（现汇率约合 93.5 万至 126.9 万元人民币）。招聘信息还特别说明，股权奖励是基本工资之外整体薪酬的重要组成部分。这意味着行政和后勤支持人员同样可以在领取工资的同时获得公司股权。Anthropic 披露，2024 年授予员工的股票期权，平均行权价为每股 1.30 美元（现汇率约合 8.7 元人民币）。Anthropic CFO 克里希纳 · 拉奥同样获得了股权激励。招股书显示，公司 2024 年向他授予 1400 万份股票期权，行权价也是每股 1.30 美元（现汇率约合 8.7 元人民币）。按照拟议 IPO 发行价计算，扣除行权成本和税款前，这些期权的内在价值约为 10 亿美元（现汇率约合 66.81 亿元人民币）。

articles.title: 3.4 万日元：哈曼卡顿发布 Allure 2 音箱，经典透明设计、60W 功率
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 19 日消息，哈曼卡顿现已在日本市场推出 Allure 2 家用音箱。新品延续 SoundSticks 经典透明设计，建议零售价 34,100 日元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 1,429 元人民币），11 月 26 日起出货。据介绍，这款音箱配备 3 个 1.5 英寸扬声器单元，以及 3.5 英寸低音单元，总功率可达 60W，频响范围为 40Hz 至 20kHz (-6dB)，信噪比 80dB(A)。同时这款音箱支持 AI Sound Boost 技术，可进一步优化声音输出，让音效更加饱满。该机兼容蓝牙 5.4 技术，最多可同时连接 2 台手机。用户可以将两台 Allure 2 音箱连接起来，构建更宽广的立体声场。当然也可以使用 Auracast 广播技术，让 2 台以上 Allure 2 同步播放音乐。此外，这款音箱还具备 360° 炫彩光效，可通过 Harman Kardon One 应用程序调整灯光效果、均衡器和其他设置。IT之家注意到，该音箱已经在国内的部分 Apple 授权专营店展出，但官方零售价并没有公布。

articles.title: 微软纳德拉：AI 代劳网购将重塑互联网生意，拒绝接入的平台恐失去机会
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 19 日消息，科技媒体 TechCrunch 昨日（11 月 18 日）发布博文，报道称在《纽约时报》DealBook 峰会上，微软首席执行官萨蒂亚 · 纳德拉（Satya Nadella）表示，能够替用户浏览商品、完成购买的 AI 智能体，可能重塑互联网的商业格局，让依赖用户访问和广告收入的平台面临重新洗牌。IT之家援引博文介绍，纳德拉认为，今天许多平台的赚钱方式，建立在人们亲自上网浏览、点击的基础上。当 AI 开始代替用户执行任务，流量如何分配、平台之间由谁向谁付费，都可能发生变化。他将这一转变比作当年互联网入口从雅虎等门户网站转向谷歌等搜索引擎。报道称，亚马逊阻止 AI 智能体访问其零售网站，限制它们替用户浏览商品和下单。纳德拉指出，如果亚马逊继续拒绝接入，而其他平台选择开放，后者就可能获得竞争优势。

articles.title: 西门子达成收购 Breker 协议，增强 SoC 验证能力
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 19 日消息，Siemens（西门子）当地时间本月 17 日宣布，已就收购 Breker Verification Systems 签署协议。这笔交易预计将于今年 12 月完成。Breker 的加入将为西门子 EDA 产品组合增强 SoC 验证能力。IT之家了解到，Breker 于 2003 年创立，总部位于美国加利福尼亚州圣何塞，致力于开发面向先进 SoC 的自动化验证解决方案。其技术被业界领先企业用于 Arm / RISC-V 微架构 SoC 平台的设计验证。西门子近期还宣布了另一笔 EDA 领域的交易，即收购 Lauterbach。

articles.title: 韩国成为全球第四个出口额破万亿美元国家，AI 芯片旺盛需求助力
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 19 日消息，据路透社报道，受全球 AI 芯片需求旺盛推动，韩国今年累计出口额突破 1 万亿美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 6.68 万亿元人民币），成为继德国、美国和中国之后，全球第四个出口额达到这一规模的国家。韩国贸易主管部门今天（19 日）宣布，截至格林尼治时间 5 时 09 分，韩国出口额突破 1 万亿美元。相比之下，去年全年出口额创下的最高纪录为 7,090 亿美元（现汇率约合 4.74 万亿元人民币）。韩国是亚洲第四大经济体，也是三星电子和 SK 海力士等全球领先芯片制造商的所在地。全球 AI 投资热潮，带动了韩国的出口和投资。不过，韩国国内消费需求仍然疲软，出口增长带来的收益尚未惠及众多家庭。高利率、高物价以及国内股市前所未有的剧烈波动，也削弱了消费者信心。韩国总统李在明在社交平台 X 发文称：“现在，我们需要把这一成就转化为可持续增长。我们将增强主要产业的竞争力，培育 AI、生物产业等新的经济增长动力。最重要的是，出口增长应该让民众的生活变得更好。我们将实现‘全民共享的增长’，让大企业和小企业、首都圈和地方都能分享经济增长的机遇与成果。”李在明政府计划设立规模达 162.3 万亿韩元（现汇率约合 8,132.85 亿元人民币）的“未来应对基金”，把芯片产业繁荣带来的超额税收用于扶持新兴增长产业、青年发展、地方建设和教育。韩国财长上月预计，在芯片出口创纪录的带动下，今年韩国经济增速有望达到 3.5% 左右，高于去年的 1%。相关阅读：《AI 芯片拉动韩国出口向万亿美元迈进，但股市暴跌拖累内需》

articles.title: Alphabet 董事长轩尼诗：英伟达找到黄仁勋接班人很有挑战性，但并非不可能
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 19 日消息，谷歌母公司 Alphabet 董事长约翰 · 轩尼诗（John Hennessy）表示，寻找英伟达前首席执行官黄仁勋的继任者将是一项艰巨任务，但合适的人选最终会出现。当地时间 17 日，轩尼诗在美国加利福尼亚州帕洛阿尔托的斯坦福大学接受《首尔经济日报》采访时表示：“我能给董事会的建议，就是再找一位优秀的 CEO。”他补充说：“找一个像黄仁勋一样出色的人就够了。”轩尼诗表示：“从公司公布的财报来看，目前经营状况非常好。公司只需要继续保持这样的表现。”当被问及是否已经有特别合适的候选人时，轩尼诗表示目前没有具体人选。不过，他指出：“问题在于，能否从公司外部找到一位愿意接任的人选。我也希望公司内部有人能够获得晋升机会。”轩尼诗评价道：“黄仁勋确实非常出色。不过，任何公司都可能遇到这样的情况。”他强调，企业必须具备应对管理层变动的能力，并在变化中继续发展。“找到一位像黄仁勋这样的人会很有挑战性，但并非不可能。”他说。据IT之家了解，轩尼诗是一名计算机科学家，曾担任斯坦福大学校长。2018 年 2 月，埃里克 · 施密特（Eric Schmidt）卸任后，他开始担任 Alphabet 董事会主席。此前，英伟达长期由黄仁勋主导公司事务，并未设置董事会主席一职。此次风波发生后，公司才转向设置董事会主席的治理架构。同一天，轩尼诗还在斯坦福大学举行的 ASI City Forum 论坛上，与 ASI Foundry 董事长李吉米（Jimmy Lee）展开对话，重点谈及韩国与美国在人工智能领域的合作关系。轩尼诗强调，韩美人工智能产业联盟必须保持稳固。他表示：“没有下一代芯片，就没有人工智能。这一联盟必须继续保持强大。”他还指出，随着全球已经形成一个紧密相连的供应链体系，各方应尽可能将更多基础设施和产业基础布局在盟友国家。

articles.content: IT之家 11 月 19 日消息，据博主 @数码闲聊站 今日爆料，某厂 Pocket 云台工程机搭载骁龙 8 Gen 5（SM8845）芯片与 200Mp 1/1.12" 云台超级主摄，目前规划明年 3-4 月与 Ultra 一同登场。该博主未在爆料中说明该机所属厂商，结合该博主此前的爆料习惯，预计该机为 vivo 旗下。据 IT 之家 6 月 3 日报道，OPPO 与 vivo 的手持 Pocket 云台相机曾被指采用 200Mp 1/1.12" 超级大底主摄，有望与哈苏、蔡司联名，内置“旗舰级”芯片并支持生态互联。影像方面，200Mp、1/1.12" 的规格与索尼 LYT901 接近。该传感器于 2025 年 11 月发布，具备约 2 亿有效像素与 1/1.12 英寸大底，采用 0.7μm 像素间距与 Quad-Quad Bayer 阵列，支持最高 4 倍传感器内置变焦与 4K 30fps 视频录制。截至发稿，该机所用传感器型号尚未确认。截至IT之家发文，官方尚未公布该机的外观设计、屏幕尺寸、电池容量与快充规格。

articles.content: IT之家 11 月 19 日消息，科技媒体 Windows Central 今天（11 月 19 日）发布博文，报道称《侠盗猎车手 VI》（GTA 6）游戏上线首日，玩家没有急着执行任务、抢车或与警方周旋，反而将大量时间花在了各种离谱又治愈的“生活玩法”上。社交平台上，最火的一段视频来自被困公海的玩家：等待片刻后，一只戴着墨镜的救援犬会驾驶水上摩托赶来，把玩家送往“狗岛”，还能获取现金和食物等补给。这段“酷狗救援”视频迅速走红，成为游戏发售首日最具传播力的片段之一。另一些玩家则选择“居家过日子”。游戏中，玩家可以挑选涂料颜色、亲手给卧室刷墙，以提升与角色露西亚的关系。有主播为了“她会不会喜欢这个颜色”反复重刷墙面，甚至花了 40 分钟纠结室内设计，令网友直呼“真实得可怕”。更贴近现实的，是游戏内置的虚拟手机。玩家可以在巨大的犯罪开放世界中“躺平刷手机”，浏览短视频、社交帖子和评论。游戏中的细节彩蛋同样密集。玩家可以给杂货店里的猫挠下巴，但如果试图抢走车主的汽车，车里的猫会立刻发起攻击；有玩家甚至被猫“逼得”把它扔出窗外。IT之家附上相关视频如下：

articles.title: 近 3 万名电动汽车车主调查：超七成认为各种误解阻碍电车普及
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 19 日消息，当地时间 18 日，据外媒 insideevs 报道，非营利组织“全球电动汽车联盟”发布的《2026 年全球电动汽车车主调查》显示，74% 的受访者认为，外界对电动汽车的错误认知是阻碍本国市场普及电动汽车的主要因素之一。相比之下，认为购车价格是主要障碍的受访者占 49%，认为公寓楼充电不便是主要障碍的占 47%。调查于 9 月至 10 月开展，共有来自 34 个国家的 29547 名电车车主参与。受访者通过电动汽车协会、志愿者和爱好者组织报名，全球统计结果则按照各国电动汽车保有量占比加权计算。IT之家提醒：调查反映的是现有车主认为哪些因素妨碍了其他人购车，并不能证明对“首购一族”来说，错误信息真的比价格更重要。调查真正揭示的是，车主如何看待实际用车体验与外界印象之间的差距。电池寿命毫不意外地成为最常被提及的误解，72% 的受访者选择了这一项。只要有人对改用电动汽车持怀疑态度，电池能用多久几乎总是绕不开的话题。此外，58% 的受访者认为电动汽车更容易起火是常见误解，45% 的人则提到了大规模普及电动汽车会导致电网崩溃的说法。说到自己的车辆，65% 的受访者并不担心电池寿命，只有 18% 表示担忧。另有 40% 的受访者认为，电车对气候并不比油车更环保，是外界普遍存在的误解之一。判断一辆车的排放水平，不能只看行驶过程，还需要计算制造和能源使用等整个生命周期的排放。生产动力电池会增加制造阶段的排放，但电动汽车在使用期间通常排放更低，足以逐步弥补前期增加的排放。至于最终能减少多少排放，还取决于当地的电力来源。

articles.title: 《GTA 6》虽大获成功，但开发团队仍担心失业
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 19 日消息，要说《GTA 6》是一款现象级成功的游戏，应该没有人会反对。这款作品预计将打破《GTA 5》创造的商业纪录，同时在 Metacritic 评分网站上与《塞尔达传说：时之笛》并列历史评分最高的游戏。然而即便如此，参与开发这款游戏的许多 Rockstar 员工，如今仍然担心自己可能失去工作。IT之家注意到，Rockstar 动画程序员内斯托尔 · 乌里亚特（Nestor Uriart）近日在英国《卫报》撰文，支持本月举行的 Rockstar Games 全体英国员工工会认证投票。他认为，成立工会是保障员工工作岗位的关键。《战地 6》以及该游戏商业表现成功后仍然发生的裁员事件，已经一次又一次地表明：对于上市公司旗下的游戏工作室而言，无论游戏销量多高、评价多好，在决定是否大规模裁员时，股东利益往往才是更重要的考量。按理说，参与开发史上规模最大的游戏之一，应该能让员工获得一定的工作保障，但 Rockstar 的情况显然并非如此。乌里亚特写道：“像这样一款游戏发售所带来的成功与喜悦，确实令人振奋。但游戏行业从业者也早已习惯了随之而来的其他后果，而且这些后果并不那么令人愉快：游戏发售前的高强度加班，以及发售后的大规模裁员。”他认为，成立工会也有助于解决 Rockstar 过去曾遭遇的有关加班文化的争议。他表示：“有了强大的工会，我们就能确保这种工作模式不会卷土重来。我们已经看到公司开始提供部分加班报酬，现在还希望继续推动行业进步，确保从业者付出的每一个工作小时都能得到相应报酬。”乌里亚特表示，目前没有任何迹象表明 Rockstar 即将裁员，但员工很难不担心公司的未来走向。他指出，整个游戏行业的工作室都在大幅缩减员工规模。据估计，过去两年间，全球游戏行业已经有约 2.4 万个工作岗位被裁撤。“这充分说明了游戏行业目前的处境：即便我和同事们正在参与开发史上规模最大的游戏，也依然担心自己会被裁员。现实是，在组织起来之前，整个行业的员工面对一波又一波席卷而来的裁员浪潮，几乎没有反抗的能力。”《GTA 6》才刚刚发售，目前还无法准确判断这款游戏最终能取得多大的商业成功。可以确定的是，其已经成为 PlayStation 和 Xbox 商店历史上预购量最高的游戏。不过，随着游戏开发工作逐渐转向发售后的维护与内容支持，参与项目的开发者担心团队规模缩减，也并非没有道理。即便打造出一款可能创造历史销售纪录的游戏，也未必能让开发者获得稳定的工作保障。

articles.title: 印度安得拉邦为硅晶圆厂开出最高 80% 政府补贴
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 19 日消息，根据印度安得拉邦政府当地时间 16 日完成修订的半导体和显示器制造政策 4.0，在该邦建设硅晶圆厂的企业可至多获得资本支出额 80% 的补贴。图源：Pexels这 80% 的补贴中 40% 来自印度中央政府，另外 40% 则来自邦级政府。安得拉邦在其它一些半导体芯片与显示投资上也采取了类似的“加倍补贴”策略，化合物、光子、传感、分立、显示项目的补贴上限是 70%，传统封装项目则可拿到 50% 补贴。根据印度当地媒体的统计，安得拉邦对硅晶圆厂的支持力度高于 65% 的奥里萨邦和泰米尔纳德邦、60% 的北方邦和中央邦、56% 的古吉拉特邦。此外，安得拉邦也将在印度国家级政策的基础上加码支持芯片设计，半导体设备与材料，组装、测试、标记、包装 (ATMP)，外包封测 (OSAT)，研发、人才。该邦还计划在 Tirupati 建设一座占地约 5,000 英亩（IT之家注：约 2,025 公顷）的半导体园区，作为涵盖整个价值链的制造和供应商集群。

articles.title: 豆包实时音视频通话模型 1.0 API 全量上线，可实现边看边听边说全模态实时交互
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 19 日消息，今天，火山引擎正式上线豆包实时音视频通话模型（SeedRealtime 1.0） API 服务，带来全模态交互的新体验。据介绍，SeedRealtime 将声音、画面、时序与表达统一到同一个端到端模型中，能在连续的多模态信息流上实时交互，带来“边看、边听、边说”的全新体验。这大大降低了传统语音级联系统依赖 ASR、VLM、TTS 等多个模块串联带来的延迟叠加和信息损耗。模型不再只是等待用户提问，而能持续理解场景变化，在合适的时机主动开口，把看、听、说纳入同一套实时决策体系，让“听到的”和“看到的”共同参与每一次实时判断与表达。IT之家注意到，SeedRealtime 原生支持声音、画面与时序信息的深度融合，既能结合场景消解同音词歧义，也能准确理解视觉中的时序指代，让所见、所闻与所说融为一体。这意味着，在多人、嘈杂、开放的真实环境中，模型不仅能看懂当前画面，还能分清说话对象、理解上下文关系，并基于多模态信息完成更准确的实时判断。无论是多人协同交流、跨语言导览，还是带视觉上下文的实时问答，交互都更自然、更完整。在多人聚餐场景中，Seed Realtime 1.0 可结合视觉、语音区分自动不同人物，记住各人身份，还能能依据多人不同需求定制旅行方案。Seed Realtime 1.0 具备持续环境感知与主动表达能力，能够在察觉关键目标出现、画面状态变化或任务节点到来时，主动进行提醒、反馈和补充，让交互从被动响应升级为主动协作。这种能力让模型可以更好适配真实业务流程。例如在设备操作、学习辅助、任务提醒等场景中，模型能够持续观察当前状态，在合适时机主动介入，而无需用户每一步都显式发问。对开发者而言，这将帮助实时 AI 应用从“会对话”进一步走向“会协助”。在机器操作场景中，Seed Realtime 1.0 看到用户将整颗咖啡豆倒入萃取手柄，及时提醒咖啡豆需要先研磨；萃取完成后，根据咖啡油脂和出液量，主动给出缩短萃取时长的建议，可在真实场景里自主点评，不用用户一步步提问。在学习场景中，Seed Realtime 1.0 能持续监控翻页画面，识别到指定章节后快速提醒用户并，并随即报出学习率、动量、权重衰减等关键配置训练参数。Seed Realtime 1.0 能够实时感知用户的对话状态与交流节奏，在适当时机自然接话、停顿与回应，并具备较强的抗干扰能力，可分辨旁人闲聊与背景噪声，不因干扰误触发。相比级联模型，Seed Realtime 1.0 的音视频对话节奏问题减少了一半，单次对话能够完整、顺畅交流的概率也有明显提升。这意味着，开发者在构建语音助手、智能硬件、陪伴式应用、实时客服等场景时，有机会获得更接近自然交流的人机互动体验。在嘈杂交通场景中，Seed Realtime 1.0 能够自动过滤机场内的无关闲聊信息，当用户询问时，调用之前看到的大屏航班信息作答，同时精准识别指示牌，主动指引旅客到达网约车上车点。在家庭场景中，妈妈在一旁忙着别的事，让 Seed Realtime 1.0 陪女儿学习动物英文。背景里爸爸正在接电话、人声不断，但模型不受影响，始终跟着女孩手指的方向实时纠音、举例造句，出声时不迟疑，受干扰时不跑偏。

articles.title: 微软 Win11 酝酿“新兴风险”功能：提醒第三方软件 / 驱动漏洞
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 19 日消息，科技媒体 Windows Latest 今天（11 月 19 日）发布博文，报道称微软正酝酿名为“新兴风险”（Emerging Risks）的 Windows 11 安全功能，用于追踪电脑上应用、驱动程序和固件中的严重漏洞，并提醒用户可采取的措施。该媒体指出微软已在 Windows 11 预览版（原文并未提及具体版本号）中测试上线相关页面，目前暂未公开推送，且相关功能有待进一步完善。根据该媒体晒出的截图，在 Windows 11 安全中心中新增“新兴风险”页面，根据描述系统检测到某个第三方应用、驱动或固件组件存在已知漏洞后，会提醒用户相关风险并展示建议处理方式。IT之家附上相关截图如下：在处理方式上，若有补丁，用户可被引导安装更新，若暂无补丁，微软可能建议卸载相关应用或驱动、或禁用受影响组件。微软对该功能的定义是：“该设备上应用、驱动程序或固件中的严重漏洞，需要关注。”系统可能对风险进行分级，帮助用户判断处理紧迫程度，并从微软及第三方渠道获取漏洞详情，辅助用户作出决定。微软确认，“新兴风险”计划面向所有 Windows 11 电脑开放，且没有额外硬件或安全设置门槛；即使用户关闭了安全启动或内存完整性，也可使用该功能。相关阅读：《微软推出 Win11 新安全检查机制：未达标情况下应用可设置拒绝运行》

articles.title: 马斯克称每次来中国都感到惊叹，透露此行还将到访特斯拉上海工厂
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 19 日消息，据澎湃新闻报道，马斯克 11 月 18 日在深圳连线出席 TomorrowX 峰会。他表示，自己是中国的粉丝，每次来都感到惊叹，鼓励大家亲自看看，此行还将到访特斯拉上海工厂。据IT之家今日早些时候报道，这是马斯克首次公开到访深圳，他于 11 月 18 日随美国代表团抵达，出席在深圳举行的 2026 年 APEC 领导人会议周相关活动。他还承诺特斯拉将继续在中国提高产量。公开资料显示，2026 年上半年，特斯拉上海超级工厂交付近 46.8 万辆，同比增长 28.4%，占特斯拉全球同期产量的 54% 以上。上海工厂同时是特斯拉全球最大的出口中心，10 月出口 59,012 辆，约占当月批发销量的 87%。相关阅读：《马斯克自称“中国超级粉丝”：首次到访深圳被震撼，特斯拉将继续在华提高产量》

articles.title: 10 月我国动力和储能电池合计产量 245.1GWh，同比增长 43.6%
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 19 日消息，今日，中国汽车动力电池产业创新联盟发布 2026 年 10 月动力电池月度信息，IT之家整理主要内容如下：产量方面：10 月，我国动力和储能电池合计产量为 245.1GWh，环比增长 3.0%，同比增长 43.6%。1-10 月，我国动力和储能电池累计产量为 2078.1GWh，累计同比增长 60.8%。销量方面：10 月，我国动力和储能电池销量为 230.4GWh，环比增长 3.4%，同比增长 38.8%。其中，动力电池销量为 159.3GWh，占总销量 69.1%，环比增长 6.7%，同比增长 28.1%；储能电池销量为 71.1GWh，占总销量 30.9%，环比下降 3.3%，同比增长 70.5%。1-10 月，我国动力和储能电池累计销量为 1912.1GWh，累计同比增长 55.1%。其中，动力电池累计销量为 1245.6GWh，占总销量 65.1%，累计同比增长 36.8%；储能电池累计销量为 666.4GWh，占总销量 34.9%，累计同比增长 106.5%。10 月，我国动力和储能电池合计出口 46.1GWh，环比增长 4.8%，同比增长 63.4%，占当月销量 20.0%。其中，动力电池出口量为 29.0GWh，占总出口量 62.9%，环比增长 2.2%，同比增长 49.4%；储能电池出口量为 17.1GWh，占总出口量 37.1%，环比增长 9.7%，同比增长 94.4%。1-10 月，我国动力和储能电池累计出口 349.0GWh，累计同比增长 53.0%，占累计销量 18.3%。其中，动力电池累计出口为 228.7GWh，占总出口量 65.5%，累计同比增长 54.0%；储能电池累计出口量为 120.3GWh，占总出口量 34.5%，累计同比增长 51.3%。装车量方面：10 月，国内动力电池装车量 99.4GWh，环比增长 14.0%，同比增长 18.2%。其中三元电池装车量 12.8GWh，占总装车量 12.9%，环比增长 3.8%，同比下降 22.8%；磷酸铁锂电池装车量 86.3GWh，占总装车量 86.9%，环比增长 15.8%，同比增长 27.8%。1-10 月，国内动力电池累计装车量 675.6GWh，累计同比增长 16.9%。其中三元电池累计装车量 110.6GWh，占总装车量 16.4%，累计同比增长 2.7%；磷酸铁锂电池累计装车量 563.5GWh，占总装车量 83.4%，累计同比增长 19.9%。

articles.title: 单日新增 200 辆，Cybercab 在特斯拉得州 Robotaxi 车队占比超一半
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 19 日消息，特斯拉单日向得克萨斯州 Robotaxi 无人驾驶出租车车队新增 200 辆 Cybercab，创下该车型单日新增数量纪录。这批专为自动驾驶打造的双座车型在得州的登记数量由此突破 750 辆。根据得克萨斯州机动车辆管理局的自动驾驶汽车登记记录，这批车辆于当地时间 11 月 17 日下午 3 时 45 分登记入册，其中包括 200 辆 Cybercab 和 1 辆 Model Y。在此次新增前，特斯拉登记在册的 Cybercab 数量自 10 月底以来一直维持在 573 辆。此次新增车辆也让特斯拉重新超过 Waymo，成为得州登记无人驾驶车辆数量最多的企业。目前，特斯拉在得州登记的无人驾驶车辆达到 1507 辆，Waymo 则为 1321 辆，双方相差 186 辆。在这批车辆登记之前，Waymo 还领先特斯拉 15 辆。特斯拉于 11 月 10 日首次在得州超过 Waymo，随后 Waymo 短暂夺回领先位置。如今，随着这批 Cybercab 集中登记，特斯拉再次反超。目前，Cybercab 已占特斯拉得州登记车队的 51.3%，具体为 773 辆，超过 Model Y 的 734 辆。Waymo 在得州的车队则包括 874 辆捷豹 I-PACE 和 447 辆 Ojai 车型。需要注意的是，车辆登记记录并未说明这些汽车具体会在哪里运营，完成登记也不意味着车辆已经开始搭载乘客。不过，此次车队扩张的时间点与特斯拉在达拉斯的部署计划较为吻合。在 10 月举行的第三季度财报电话会议上，特斯拉人工智能负责人埃隆 · 埃卢斯瓦米（Ashok Elluswamy）曾表示：“下个月，我们将在达拉斯启动服务。”上周末发布的一段视频还显示，达拉斯一处停车场内停放着 50 多辆 Cybercab，附近另有一辆汽车运输车，车上也装载着更多车辆。不过，特斯拉尚未公布当地服务的具体启动日期。达拉斯已经是特斯拉 Robotaxi 业务最繁忙的市场之一。从 11 月 11 日起，当地的 Model Y Robotaxi 已开始全天候在没有安全员坐在驾驶座的情况下运行。根据特斯拉发布的首份 Robotaxi 安全报告，今年 1 月 22 日至 10 月 18 日期间，达拉斯 Robotaxi 车队在没有安全监控员的情况下累计行驶 608130 英里，仅次于奥斯汀。自 9 月 Cybercab 加入 Robotaxi 服务以来，公众能够乘坐 Cybercab 的服务目前仍仅限于奥斯汀。车队规模持续扩大之际，特斯拉也在调整工厂产能，将更多资源转向 Cybercab 生产。公司计划在 2027 年夏末之前逐步结束得州超级工厂的 Cybertruck 生产，为 Cybercab 腾出产能。本周，特斯拉还宣布将投资 30 亿欧元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 219.84 亿元人民币）扩建柏林超级工厂，并新建一座生产设施。按照规划，该设施从 2029 年开始投产后，年产能最高可达 100 万辆 Cybercab。此外，Cybercab 很快也将交付给私人消费者。上周，特斯拉开始邀请部分指定客户购买这款车型，用于个人出行，售价为 29,990 美元（现汇率约合 20 万元人民币），同时要求用户每月支付 299 美元（现汇率约合 1,998 元人民币）的自动驾驶订阅费用。特斯拉计划从 12 月开始交付，首批交付范围覆盖 Robotaxi 目前运营的得州五座城市。

articles.title: AI4S青年志②丨赋澈生物王子龙：实验室里的「企业家」
articles.content: 同时拥有理工科训练、结构生物学功底，和系统商科思维的创业者，在AI4S领域里并不常见。    作者丨周蕾    编辑丨岑峰                                                                                                       【编者按】AI4S有时给人“雷声大雨点小”之感，是因为不少人把AI当成了目的本身，拿着锤子满世界找钉子，对科研周期与商业回报的错配却无知无觉。“AI4S青年志”第二篇，我们关注一个可能破解AI4S落地困局的样本。一篇论文，通常只需要2-4位审稿人。但当《Nature Biotechnology》的编辑们打开一篇来自加州大学伯克利分校的投稿时，他们很快意识到，2-4位远远不够。为了覆盖这篇论文涉及的每一个学科，编辑们前后邀请的审稿人数量已经来到了两位数。论文横跨四个领域：合成生物学、材料科学、计算化学，以及技术经济学与碳排放核算。审稿人们上来就说：他们只能看懂属于自己的那一部分，无法对其他部分做出评价。学术论文通常像一辆概念车，但这篇论文，却被以量产车的标准来严苛审视。例如论文已经在实验室里证明，生物反应器中，新型塑料单体的滴度达到了1.84克每升——这是一个符合学术发表标准的数字。但一位材料学背景的审稿人直接追问：“如果这个平台要走向产业化，至少要让我看到几十克每升的可能性。”这些质疑，同时关乎科学和商业。而回应它的人，需要同时听懂四种语言。最终，四个不同领域的专家全部认可了这篇论文，编辑也点了头，论文在今年夏天成功刊发。这篇论文的署名栏里，第一作者只有一个名字：王子龙。在AI for Science的创业浪潮里，跨学科背景并不稀奇。计算机出身的人去学材料，化学出身的人去写代码，这样的故事比比皆是。但像王子龙这样，同时拥有扎实的理工科训练、结构生物学的底层功底，以及从本科阶段就开始的系统商科思维，并且能把这一切翻译成彼此能听懂的语言——这种人在AI4S创业者中，并不常见。借着论文刊发的机会，雷峰网AI科技评论和王子龙完成了一次两个多小时的越洋连线，从中山大学逸仙班的经济学课堂聊到Jay Keasling的实验室，从主动拒绝创业风口聊到放弃教职、投身产业，试图还原这位AI4S青年科学家，在他过去二十年里的每一次关键选择。01像“爱迪生”的底色王子龙儿时的梦想，是成为爱迪生那样的科学家。长大后他意识到，原来爱迪生不光是科学家，同时也是一名商人，而他恰好也将自己培养出了科学家+企业家的双重能力结构。这种能力结构的雏形，最早要追溯到本科时期。王子龙所就读的中大逸仙班，准入门槛极高，采用多学科混合培养的方式，除了数物化生的理工科内容，还有专门开设的经济学课程，由岭南学院的教授整套授课。加之出生于经商家庭，从事零售和分销，王子龙对商业实践已有着十几年的认知。逸仙班的课业负担不轻，但当时的多学科培养，尤其是经济学方面的训练，直到今天仍然在为他的商业工作带来极大的帮助。一方面经济学带给他反直觉的思维和理论，帮助他避免踩坑；另一方面，这套训练也为一位纯科学家在做商业谈判、市场判断时，提供了底气。“基本的商业逻辑、经济逻辑我们都清楚，对外融资、谈合作的时候，精神面貌是不一样的。”2011年，中山大学首次参加MIT创办的iGEM（国际基因工程机器大赛），正在读大三、准备出国留学的王子龙，正是当时参赛的领队和对外主讲人。队伍最终闯入了全球决赛。在MIT的讲台上，他要用英语向评委解释团队的成果；回到实验室，他又得和队友一起解决具体的科学问题。这个比赛最终帮他敲开了合成生物学认知的大门。也是在这个时期，他读到了一篇经典论文：用大肠杆菌和酵母菌全合成青蒿素前体。屠呦呦当年发现的青蒿素，在合成生物学的方法下，得以实现低成本、大规模的生产。而这位论文的作者Jay Keasling，后来成为了他在伯克利的导师。“我们可以改造自然界的微生物，让它们为人类所用，实现不同的功能。”合成生物学最底层的定义，是让每个基因的设计模块化，“像拼乐高一样拼基因，拼出不同的形态和功能。”王子龙被合成生物学深深

articles.title: NEBench R1: a Reasoning Benchmark for Evaluating Nuclear Domain Competence in Large Language Models
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21682v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being explored for knowledge-intensive and safety-critical applications in nuclear engineering. However, existing nuclear-domain benchmarks provide limited content coverage or focus primarily on answer accuracy without systematically evaluating the quality of the underlying reasoning. This study introduces NEBench R1, a reasoning-oriented benchmark comprising 7,546 unique multiple-choice questions extracted from U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) reactor operator licensing examinations covering 18 nuclear facilities. Each question is classified according to the NRC Knowledge and Abilities catalogs and accompanied by an official explanation serving as a reference for reasoning evaluation. Six LLMs were evaluated, with overall accuracy ranging from 34.0% to 73.9% across three distinct performance tiers. To assess reasoning quality, an LLM-based judge evaluated correctly answered responses

articles.title: Chain-of-Thought Controllability Can Reduce Chain-of-Thought Monitorability
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21799v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Chain-of-thought (CoT) monitoring is a promising tool for detecting hidden goals, off-task behavior, and other failures in AI agents. One risk is that models could deliberately shape their reasoning to make it opaque to monitors. We stress-test this risk through persona-control training: supervised fine-tuning on mathematical reasoning traces rewritten in the voices of diverse personas. This induces a broader ability to control CoT, even though training contains no monitor-evasion examples. In covert side-task evaluations, traces in which a gpt-oss-20b model organism completes the hidden side task contain less monitorable evidence than the base model's. Averaged across evaluations and CoT lengths, weighted by side-task-success counts, the CoT monitorability metric g-mean$^2$ falls from 0.94 for the base model to 0.68 for the model organism without a hiding instruction, and to 0.22 when explicitly instructed to hide. articles.title: How Much of SAR Vehicle Recognition Is the Vehicle? Background Shortcuts, Angle Gaps and Partial Libraries on MSTAR and ATRNet-STAR
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21827v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Deep networks score near 99% on the MSTAR vehicle benchmark, and the newer ATRNet-STAR benchmark was built to be harder. We ask how much of these scores comes from the vehicle itself. With a modern network (ConvNeXt-Small, 3 seeds) we first reproduce the known MSTAR result: with the central 96x96 pixels zeroed out, accuracy is still 73.3% (chance 10%). The same shortcut is present in ATRNet-STAR, which was collected across several scenes: with the vehicle removed, accuracy is 63.3% on the 40-class SOC split (chance 2.5%). Under the official scene-change split, the background stops helping and starts hurting. Accuracy is 22.8% on full chips and 30.8% when only the vehicle is shown. A SAR foundation model, SARATR-X, leans on the background more than ConvNeXt does (+4 to +6 points with the vehicle removed, in every seed) and does not solve the scene change. articles.title: Auditors Struggle to Catch Sabotage In End-to-End Transcripts of AI Safety Research
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21832v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: As AI systems are increasingly used to automate AI R&D, misaligned systems could sabotage research intended to improve model safety and alignment. To stress-test defenses against such sabotage, we use a human expert as a proxy saboteur on AI safety research. We conduct a red-team/blue-team game where a human researcher runs AI safety experiments from scratch and auditors try to tell which were sabotaged and how. Given access to the full research transcript and the ability to run experiments, human auditors mostly fail to distinguish sabotaged from benign research: they achieve an AUROC of 0.59, not significantly better than chance, and fully identify the specific sabotage in only 17% of cases. Despite not being allowed to run experiments, the best frontier models outperform human auditors (Fable 5.1: AUROC 0.73, 32% full identification) within noise and weaker models perform comparably. articles.title: Language Models Can Rewrite Their Own Weights
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21885v2 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A language model is trained once and frozen. Making it better takes another training run, or a prompt, a harness or extra computation at inference that is gone once the task ends. We show a third way: to our knowledge for the first time, a language model rewrites its own weights by its own reasoning and becomes better, with no gradients and no training. We call this self-rewriting: the model is its own optimizer. In earlier work, a frontier model edited a much smaller one; here an open 27B model, given its weights, its graded answers and the ability to run itself, diagnoses its own failure and rewrites the weights behind it. It surpasses itself: its own edit makes it 6.6 points more accurate on problems it never saw. It keeps getting better: it tests its edits on practice problems and submits only what works, each edit improving on the last, and over eight consecutive sessions its accuracy only rises. articles.title: DNeo: Your Parallel Draft Model Needs Better Target Feature Encoding
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21925v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Speculative-diffusion decoding uses a small parallel drafter model to generate b draft tokens in one forward pass, which then undergo parallel verification via a larger target model. Faster inference can be achieved when multiple draft tokens pass verification simultaneously. Recent parallel draft architectures (DFlash, DSpark) improve draft quality by conditioning on rich features computed by the target, through a mechanism known as feature encoding. However, standard feature encoding mechanisms have three limitations: (1) they are lossy, applying encoding projections that are destructive to the underlying target feature-space via a discovered effect known as residual mixing, (2) they are memory-less, with no record of previously processed proposals, and (3) they utilize features sampled uniformly from across the target layers, omitting important hidden states. articles.title: SLED: Sensor SLicing from Edge to Datacenter
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21937v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Modern sensing systems generate large volumes of heterogeneous data streams from multiple sensor modalities, increasing reliance on datacenters for computation, artificial intelligence/superintelligence (AI/SI) inference, and AI/SI training. Each sensor stream may have different network and compute requirements depending on its type and data volume. However, current wireless systems typically allocate resources at the device level, leading to contention among co-located sensor streams, where bulk data transfers may starve latency-critical telemetry. To this end, this paper introduces Sensor Slicing (SL). SL provides deterministic, medium access control (MAC)-level isolation for individual sensors within a single user equipment (UE) in open radio access networks (O-RAN). articles.title: Conserved Verdicts, Drifting Commitments: Identifying Harmful Overthinking
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21946v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A reasoning model that has reached a correct answer can lose it by continuing to think. Deciding whether to stop means comparing two probabilities at the same point of a chain: that the answer the model would give if stopped now is correct (its commitment), and that the answer it will finish with is correct (its verdict). We show that the verdict alone, which is what final-correctness probes estimate, cannot make this comparison. As a forecast of a fixed outcome it has no predictable drift, whether continuing helps or hurts. The commitment-verdict gap equals the expected remaining change in answer quality and the accuracy gained by stopping. A second identity splits any accuracy-versus-budget curve into answer change within chains and change in which chains are still running. We measure both on MATH-500. articles.title: Honest Brokers in AI Regulation: How Public Comments Introduce Evidence to Regulators
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21948v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The regulation of Artificial Intelligence is susceptible to various forms of capture by industry actors that hold undue influence over the policymaking process, due in part to their information advantage in developing these technologies. In the following paper, we investigate the roles of public commenters in providing evidence to potential regulation in the USA. We build a corpus of 40 potential regulations, and 2,664 public comments submitted by a variety of stakeholders. We computationally process these texts to extract evidence meant to inform regulators, in the form of formal citations and informal references. We find significant differences in the type and amount of evidence supplied: Holding comment length constant, business commenters introduce altogether less evidence, and government, university, and civil society commenters provide significantly more research and legal sources. articles.title: DiscoveryAgent: A Framework for Scientist-centric Agentic AI
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21950v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: AI agents can assist scientific research, but balancing autonomous investigation with scientists' ability to inspect and redirect ongoing work remains a central design challenge. We present DiscoveryAgent, a domain-agnostic, scientist-centric system that combines autonomous investigation with scientist-directed hypothesis steering. Scientists select, refine, or replace hypotheses between research rounds, while audit agents interrogate checkpointed records to trace claims, reproduce analyses, and inform subsequent decisions. Across two predictive modeling tasks, DiscoveryAgent produced the best variable-star classifier among evaluated baselines and, with scientist steering, a protein variant-effect predictor surpassed by only one of 106 ProteinGym baselines. articles.title: WebAgents: Unbundling Agent Creation, Hosting, and Execution for an Agent-Native Web
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21978v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models are moving from isolated assistants toward autonomous agents that can plan, use tools, and coordinate with others, motivating an emerging Agentic Web of independently developed agents and services. Realizing this vision requires agent behavior to move across creators, hosts, and runtimes without coupling publication to a particular execution environment or transferring authority over user resources. We introduce WebAgents, which unbundles these roles through a signed agent.pkg that carries portable workflows, skills, schemas, and resource requirements. An OpenClaw-based agent-native browser/runtime verifies the package, obtains authorization, and binds it at run time to user-controlled models, tools, permissions, and budgets, while hosts distribute the public program and may retain private services server-side. articles.title: KV-LTM: Persistent Per-Session KV Caches as Long-Term Memory for Personal Assistants
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21998v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Personal assistants accumulate months of conversations, but today's long-term memory stacks put derivation or selection between a question and its evidence. In a system-level comparison on LongMemEval, two commercial assistants scored well below the same model reading the history offline [1], consistent with, but not isolating, content loss between write and read. We propose KV-LTM: a memory tier storing each session's raw text plus its KV cache under a fixed reader model, answering by restoring cached sessions and appending the question. KV-LTM is complementary to, not a replacement for, retrieval and indexing. Text is the memory of record; the cache is a recompute-free prefill accelerator, degrading gracefully to text. We specify the design: storage record, budget-derived retention, append-only read path, and bounded aggregation. articles.title: On Formal Counterfactual Explanations
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.22010v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Counterfactual explanations are often seen as counterfactual conditionals under closest-world semantics, requiring one to reason over all minimally distant counterexamples. In contrast, formal XAI typically relies on feature-based abductive explanations (AXps) and contrastive explanations (CXps), which admit efficient computation and a minimal hitting-set duality. This paper bridges these perspectives by (i) characterizing closest-world counterfactual explanations explicitly as a disjunctive normal form over all minimally distant counterexample instances, and (ii) introducing conjunctive counterfactual explanations (CFXps), a subclass of counterfactual antecedents restricted to conjunctions of feature literals that guarantee prediction change. Abstract: Agent Skills, file-based packages of procedural knowledge that a coding agent can discover and load on demand, are now shipped by every major agent harness, yet the evidence for how much they help comes almost entirely from settings in which the right Skill is hand-picked for the task and the agent starts from a blank slate. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.22030v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: An agent resource's value depends on its backbone and companion resources and is known only after execution. Token-based generators remain tied to their training catalog, while independent resource scoring misses complementarities and reused bundles target other tasks. We formulate Task-Conditioned Agent Resource Composition (AgentComposition): jointly selecting a backbone model and a tool-skill bundle to maximize end-to-end execution utility. Our Retrieval-Grounded Bundle-Aware Agent Generation retrieves candidate resources and past configurations of similar tasks. A fine-tuned generator reads resource descriptions and recombines candidates through constrained beam search, allowing new resources without retraining. A bundle-aware critic ranks complete configurations using a large language model (LLM) teacher and historically successful configurations as execution proxies, and adapts to execution feedback when available. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.22033v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as autonomous shopping agents that process multimodal product listings (consisting of visual and text data) and recommend purchases on behalf of consumers. Naturally, one might assume that models with more thinking power would make higher-quality purchasing decisions. To test this belief, we ask two questions about such agents: does asking a model to think harder make it choose better products, and does the confidence it reports tell us the likelihood it may be wrong? We benchmark ten frontier models on three product-choice benchmarks built from WebShop, Amazon's SQID and Wayfair's WANDS platforms to see if LLMs with more thinking power actually make better-quality product purchase decisions. articles.title: A Hybrid Exact-Heuristic Solver for the Integrated Passenger and Parcel Transportation Problem
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.22043v2 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We describe the solver we submitted to the second round of the SOICT 2026 contest on the Integrated Passenger and Parcel Transportation problem, a selective pickup-and-delivery routing problem with time windows, open routes and heterogeneous taxis. The solver is a single-file, standard-library Python program that combines (i) a constant-time insertion test based on latest-arrival slack, (ii) greedy insertion, local search and an Adaptive Large Neighborhood Search (ALNS) with simulated-annealing acceptance, and (iii) an exact route-selection engine that enumerates, for every taxi, the best feasible route for each request set and then solves the resulting set-packing problem by branch-and-bound strengthened with route-based large neighborhood search, Lagrangian bounds and reduced-cost fixing. articles.title: MedGuardBench: A Patient-Oriented Benchmark for Personalized Guardrail Development
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.22069v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Safety is personal: the same action can be safe for one person but unsafe for another. Yet current guardrails judge content without considering who is affected. Using medication safety, we introduce \textit{patient-conditioned medication guarding}, which predicts a safety verdict and 17 risk categories from a patient profile and prescription. We release \textbf{MedGuardBench}, a drug-disjoint benchmark of 5{,}001 scenarios across 87 medications. We find that standard guardrails rely on surface cues, such as wording and profile presence, rather than patient facts. articles.title: Can You Undo It? Reversibility Classes for AI Agent Actions
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.22075v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Tool-using AI agents change files, databases, access rights and public information, yet permission to call a tool does not establish whether a mistake can be undone. We present Reversibility Classes, a declared five-level vocabulary with argument-sensitive rules, conservative defaults and an explicit prior-state capture contract. The pinned implementation and evidence-linked registry cover 536 tools across 20 MCP servers. All 738 rule-case checks conform to declared expectations, while native annotation mapping differs from draft registry labels for 118 of 481 comparable tools. One AI-assisted reviewer approves 148 ratings, 75 matching the registry; this is not independent agreement. On 2,158 recorded runs, the implemented session guard gates the associated action in all 29 attributable attack-positive runs, compared with 18 for a read/write proxy, while adding nine approval points across 1,209 benign runs. articles.title: When Lower Harm Misleads: Auditing Concept Corrections
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.22084v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: An expert who corrects a concept prediction, such as a BI-RADS descriptor in breast ultrasound, expects the diagnosis to improve. Objectives that reduce the harm of such corrections are judged by harm and accuracy, yet harm also falls when a model responds less to every correction or starts from a worse uncorrected prediction, the reference for harm. We propose a correction audit, a reproducible evaluation protocol that separates these explanations: it splits each correction into harm and useful gain on identical events, separates the starting prediction from the correction response, and compares objectives with amplitude baselines matched in source harm. Abstract: Hysteresis is a complex nonlinear phenomenon characterized by memory dependence, path dependence, and, in many physical systems, degradation, non-congruency, asymmetry, and rate dependence. Particular attention is given to their mechanisms for representing memory, network architectures, activation functions, training algorithms, treatment of deterioration and rate dependence, and applications to nonlinear structural and material systems. Abstract: The UK distribution-cable monitoring sector is data-rich but framework-poor: each Distribution Network Operator (DNO) collects megabytes of telemetry per asset per day, but there is no public benchmark dataset, no shared reference model, and no commonly agreed evaluation protocol for benchmarking sectoral, data-intensive models for operational decision support; notably for maintenance planning and prioritisation. articles.title: Biologically-Inspired Spike Encoding and Optimization for Spiking Neural Networks
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23242v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) offer theoretical energy-efficiency advantages over conventional deep networks, but realizing these advantages on vision tasks requires sparse spike representations that naive rate-coding methods fail to provide. We combine biologically motivated spike-encoding schemes with two training improvements: Rouser adaptive-threshold surrogate gradients and Kronecker-Factored Approximate Curvature (K-FAC) second-order optimization. The spike encoding schemes experimented with are rate coding, latency coding, DVS-style delta modulation, and Difference-of-Gaussians (DoG) filtering. Experiments on MNIST and Fashion-MNIST demonstrate that biologically inspired encoders yield the largest accuracy gains in capacity-constrained regimes and serve as an effective parameter-efficiency lever. Abstract: Goemans conjectured that any fractional single-source flow could be converted into an unsplittable flow without increasing total cost and while increasing any arc load by at most the largest demand. However, the interaction did not reveal why this particular topology and its demand, fractional-flow, and cost choices work together, whether the example belongs to a broader family, or which structural features determine where counterexamples can occur. It also left unclear why the AI-assisted search succeeded where earlier human efforts had not. In this paper, we develop a forward counterexample construction pipeline. articles.title: Response-Relevant Information Is Not Sufficient for Neural Training-State Equivalence
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23245v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Response-relevant information is not sufficient evidence that two neural networks are in the same training state. We define training-state equivalence operationally: two checkpoints are equivalent, relative to an intervention family and horizon, if they respond alike when training is perturbed and continues. On fresh runs of a one-layer transformer learning modular addition, response to a weight-decay pulse is highly reproducible relative to between-checkpoint differences (rho_state = 0.934 at 500 steps), establishing the target as measurable. Fifteen descriptors of weight spectra, representation geometry and optimiser geometry carry within-run response-relevant information beyond weight norm and loss on a development dataset, predicting held-out response deviation across seed blocks. articles.title: Chebyshev Polynomial Zonotope Abstractions for Certified Reachability of Learning-Enabled Systems
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23246v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Nearly all current methods for computing reachable sets of nonlinear dynamics propagate them with truncated Taylor expansions plus rigorous remainders. The expansion is pointwise: once its argument is a whole set rather than a point, one polynomial must stay accurate across that set, and it reaches only as far as its disc of convergence. The limit binds hardest on the rational terms and sigmoid gates of modern controllers: smooth as these look on the real line, in the complex plane they blow up at points just off the real axis, closer as a gate sharpens, and those points cap the set width a Taylor expansion can cover, most tightly on the switching surface where the controller decides. We prove a dichotomy: no Taylor degree certifies sets wider than that cap, while a Chebyshev abstraction of equal degree, anchored to the whole set in the same polynomial-zonotope pipeline, has no cap and gains width at a geometric rate in degree. articles.title: Budgeted Proper Loss Design for Uncertain Decision Thresholds
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23247v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A binary probability estimate may be used by several decision makers with different error costs. Proper scoring rules can emphasize selected probability thresholds, but a single average threshold distribution need not give a good worst-case regret guarantee. We study the choice of a proper loss when the threshold distribution belongs to a finite specified family. Among integrable loss weights with a positive pointwise floor and a fixed total mass, we derive the weight that minimizes the sharp, distribution-free multiplier from surrogate regret to threshold-averaged decision regret. The solution clips a rescaled upper envelope of the threshold densities at the prescribed floor; its normalization is found by a one-dimensional root search. We give proofs of sharpness, optimality, and stability under density misspecification, as well as a limitation for atomic threshold laws. Abstract: Generative recommendation (GR) inference differs substantially from conventional LLM serving, featuring long input sequences, wide beam search, and only a few fixed output tokens. Abstract: The rapid development of materials machine learning relies on large-scale, heterogeneous datasets, yet model reliability is often compromised by imperfect data from diverse experiments, simulations, and database integration. Such problems are difficult to identify because corrupted samples may remain statistically plausible rather than appearing as explicit outliers. In this paper, we propose a confidence-based materials data quality assessment framework that integrates domain knowledge with graph-structured learning. Abstract: Quantization is an effective technique to reduce memory storage, computation complexity and power for Transformers, and the binarization of the weights is important for meeting these requirements. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23362v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: LLM-based multi-agent systems (MAS) rely on not only individual agent behaviors but also the interactions that connect agents, including message exchanges and task dependencies. Existing MAS safeguards mainly perform agent-level anomaly detection, which becomes insufficient when failures originate from agent interactions and detected anomalies do not necessarily reveal their true sources. To address this limitation, we propose \textbf{TRACE-MAS}, a finer-grained framework for diagnosing and repairing MAS failures. TRACE-MAS learns normal collaborative execution patterns from benign trajectories and detects deviations in agent state changes, message transitions, and task dependency evolutions. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23388v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Post-training quantization is the standard way to serve large language models at low cost. However, the best quantization recipe differs across models and precisions. As a result, experts must redesign it for every new model, which is time-consuming and often sub-optimal. Fortunately, an LLM agent can take over this design by refining the recipe over rounds of building and evaluating candidates, so that more rounds lead to better recipes. However, evaluating one quantized reasoning model takes tens of GPU-hours, and combining methods from different codebases means porting each to the new architecture by hand. We present QDA, a system in which an agent designs the recipe for each model and precision. articles.content:

Abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) trains a student language model to match a teacher model based on its own generations. When using OPD, one must choose whether to apply it at the sequence or token level and which divergence to minimize. Toward addressing this gap, we theoretically analyze how the choice of OPD objective governs which tokens are prioritized, in what order, and how efficiently. Our analysis reveals that sequence-level OPD exhibits a future agreement bias, which myopic token-level objectives avoid. Abstract: Landmark diffusion (Roseland) computes a diffusion-map-style spectral embedding from the singular value decomposition of a degree-normalized data-to-landmark kernel matrix, at a cost far below that of full diffusion maps. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23427v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Plasticity and stability in continual learning are typically studied at the entire-model level and in a task-agnostic manner, yet prior work has reported divergent conclusions across settings. Inspired by cognitive distinctions between declarative and procedural memory, we instead study how plasticity and stability vary across transformer modules and task types. In a controlled synthetic environment with clean measurement, we show a double dissociation: query-key (QK) and value-output (VO) projections are the most plastic on procedural tasks, whereas MLPs are the most plastic on declarative memorization. Stability, however, does not simply mirror plasticity: when learning a new procedure, updating QK retains over half of the stored declarative memory, while updating MLPs retains far less and updating VO loses roughly four-fifths. Abstract: Background: Crisis helplines are essential to mental health systems but are often understaffed and underfunded. Abstract: Deployed LLMs field hundreds of millions of conversations a day and refuse a non-trivial fraction of user requests, yet the user-side cost of refusal, whether users disengage and by how much, is unmeasured on any production model: a blind spot for the consumer-facing platforms built on them. A/B-testing refusal is ethically and operationally constrained on frontier-lab products and unavailable to third-party platforms deploying these models through a fixed API. We introduce RAW, a method that uses LLM stochasticity as a natural experiment: at near-identical prompts in any existing log, the same model sometimes refuses and sometimes does not, and that variation identifies the causal user-side effect of refusal. Abstract: Estimating full-night electroencephalography (EEG) spectrograms from peripheral measurements could extend EEG-informed sleep analysis to recordings acquired without EEG. Abstract: We present Limite 1B - Violetto, a one-billion-parameter model designed for high-throughput mathematical reasoning. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21669v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Masked diffusion models repeatedly predict provisional tokens before a sampler decides which predictions become permanent. Existing inference-time steering methods primarily modify activations, logits, or denoising trajectories, while treating this commitment policy as a fixed decoding detail. We instead study token commitment as a diffusion-specific control surface and separate it into two decisions: which tokens to commit and how many tokens to commit at each step. Abstract: Realistic user simulation enables the study of human interactions when direct experimentation is costly or potentially harmful. Abstract: Language models are increasingly asked where real actors stand: what a party's platform prioritises, what an institution has committed to. Such judgments are gradable, carrying both an order and a magnitude. Nearly every benchmark that tests them asks about one entity at a time, then reads that score as the model's knowledge of the domain. Order and magnitude, however, need not be acquired together. Text about social entities carries far more comparison than measurement, so a model may hold a dependable ordering with no anchored scale beneath it. We ask whether a model can place a documented social position on a scale or only order the actors it compares, and what that means for how such knowledge is measured. Abstract: Automatic assignment of ICD-10 codes from short clinical diagnosis text is a practical medical text classification and normalization task. Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have shown strong performance on medical question answering and diagnostic reasoning benchmarks. Abstract: We present the Autoregressive View Model (AVM), which generates a scene as a stream of views without constructing an explicit 3D representation. AVM retrieves relevant views from inputs and generated history to form a bounded active context. Abstract: Attention maps cheaply show where a vision-language model (VLM) looks, but attention sinks make them unreliable for localization. Contrasting the question with a generic prompt suppresses sinks, yet only some layers localize the queried object. Existing methods find these layers with box annotations or fixed rules. We show that attention itself can identify them. A question changes how much a head attends to the image and where this attention goes. The two effects separate exactly, and the second, measured in bits on unlabeled questions, indicates which layers localize. WhereBits turns these where-to-look bits into a layer prior and combines it with per-head contrastive scores. Abstract: Biometric recognition in surveillance, video, and web imagery must contend with extreme variation in pose, blur, illumination, occlusion, and distance, where visual quality metrics fail to predict whether inputs are recognizable to the deployed encoder. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23450v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Water does not just tint an underwater photograph; it rewrites it. Each pixel mixes attenuated scene radiance, backscattered light, and scene light scattered forward on its way to the camera, and many combinations of scene and water explain the same pixels. Most Gaussian-splatting methods for underwater scenes model only the first two effects and remove the water by dividing by a transmission that decays exponentially with range, so their inversion gain grows without bound. We present NIRJALA (Sanskrit for "without water"), a 3D Gaussian Splatting framework that recovers water-free appearance and geometry together. TRIVENI, a three-path image formation model, adds a range-saturating forward-scattering term to direct transmission and backscatter; we prove that this keeps the inversion gain bounded at every range and bound how errors in the estimated backscatter and attenuation propagate into the recovered colours. Abstract: Training 3D vision-language models (VLMs) on large medical imaging datasets collected across institutions is constrained by data quality. Vast, uncurated pools of image-report pairs are characterized by redundancy, class imbalance, and cross-institutional heterogeneity. Abstract: Vision-language-action models (VLAs) encode images with 2D encoders that capture little 3D structure. A common approach is to feed the policy estimated depth, but a UAV chooses its own altitude, must judge distances tens of meters away, where monocular depth is less reliable, and must relate its forward and downward views. Abstract: Put a monocular mesh estimator behind every camera of a calibrated rig, and the reconstructed bodies land a meter or more apart. The cause is geometric: each estimate sits at the depth implied by a focal length the network assumed, not the one the camera has. It then fuses the views one point at a time, under a Gaussian error whose precision follows each viewing ray. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23606v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Backward-compatible retrieval enables a new encoder to query the gallery that an old model has already encoded, so that a cross-modal retrieval system can be upgraded without re-encoding billions of items. Existing compatible methods either fit the old query and stay near the accuracy of the old model, or run the old and the new encoder for every query. We propose VIBRA, which matches relevance on the old gallery, corrects the errors of a single model with the barycenter of several views, which is itself a query in the old space, and trains the new encoder to inherit this consensus, so that models absent at deployment still shape every query. We show that the barycenter gains margin over the average of its views exactly when their hardest irrelevant items differ, and we characterize the share of this gain that one encoder can reach. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23615v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In weight-space programming, a language model edits a network's weights directly, without gradients. We ask what a successful repair of this kind relies on. We plant faults in the weights of two vision-language models, SmolVLM-256M and LFM2-VL-450M, and check each edit made by a coding agent against the original weights. Without being told where to look, the agent finds rescaled rows in the projector and noise in the vision encoder of both models, infers the unknown scale factors, restores most or all of the rescaled weights to their exact original values, and returns accuracy to near its original level; programs that it writes from such weights repair unseen checkpoints of the same model without feedback. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23616v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: One-step flow maps are increasingly used as posterior samplers, where the point of sampling is the uncertainty that the samples carry. We find that the one-step sampler loses this uncertainty and becomes less stable. Compared with multi-step samples of the same network, its samples lose variance and decorrelate. Supervising the one-step jump directly makes this worse; the samples collapse further toward the conditional mean and break down when training is extended. We trace both failures to the locations where training places its pairs of start and end times. Only pairs on the diagonal of the time triangle receive targets from data, and the pair used for one-step sampling is either left unsupervised or supervised on an island, a set of pairs that the self-consistency identity does not connect to the diagonal, where the objective neither determines the one-step map nor anchors its training. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23499v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Autoregressive vision-language-action (VLA) models predict discrete action tokens with the next-token objective of their vision-language backbone, so the action tokenizer defines the interface between the policy and the robot. In bimanual manipulation, the two arms share a repertoire of movements yet coordinate through complementary roles, and an action representation should capture both. However, most existing tokenizers encode both arms as a single concatenated action vector, in which motion patterns common to the two arms are not shared and cross-arm dependencies remain entangled within each token. The policy must therefore learn both aspects implicitly. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23502v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We introduce TAG (Testbed for Autonomous Games), a compact, low-cost robotic platform for studying learning and control in physically coupled dynamical systems. TAG combines an actively tilted and steered ball-in-maze board with a top-mounted rotary inverted pendulum. The pendulum's reaction torque and vibration disturb the board and marble, while the board's tilt, driven by the maze-solving policy, simultaneously disturbs the pendulum's balance. The main challenge in learning control policies for each subsystem is accounting for the impact of one subsystem's dynamics on the other's learning process. To address this challenge, we present complementary reinforcement learning paradigms, leveraging model-based and model-free approaches to learn the control policies for the maze and pendulum, respectively. Abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models look saturated on LIBERO, yet most of them fall apart on LIBERO-PRO as soon as an object moves or the instruction asks for something new. We argue that what is missing is not scale but decoupling.
  In these policies, what to do is tied to where things were during training, to the scene around them and to the wording of the instruction. We cut these ties in two places. In the data, LIBERO demonstrations are re-arranged by general rules: every object and fixture is moved and rotated, tasks are carried into other environments and onto other surfaces, and every instruction is paraphrased. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23531v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Centimeter-scale robots are promising for urban search and rescue because they can enter confined spaces that are inaccessible or unsafe for humans. However, their small size limits obstacle traversal after deployment. This paper presents the RESCUE Jumper, a 125 g mobile robot with a 6.2 cm width and 6.2 cm diameter wheels that combines ground rolling with jumping to traverse steps and gaps that exceeds its rolling capability. The RESCUE Jumper uses its two actuators for both rolling mode and jumping by reversing the direction of wheel motion. Forward wheel motion enables rolling, while reverse wheel motion winds a spring steel tail to store elastic potential energy and release it for jumping. The RESCUE Jumper varies tail winding speed to control jump direction, transitioning from backward to forward jumps as winding speed increases from 0.75 rad/s to 8.73 rad/s. Abstract: Many learning-based approaches for deformable linear objects (DLOs) rely on simplified deformation models that neglect dynamic effects and the mechanical response of the objects, limiting their applicability to lightweight, compliant objects and slow motions. articles.content:

Abstract: Symbolic methods make robot designs interpretable but often overlook continuous geometry; learned methods handle geometry but offer less transparent structure. We introduce a typed production grammar that uses case-role relations, parameter inheritance, and specificity-based rule arbitration to generate both manipulation skills and robot morphologies. A geometric realization map translates grammar composition into transformations in SE(3), behaving as a monoid homomorphism when inheritance is inactive and exhibiting a measurable defect when inheritance is enabled. The grammar provides a compact representation, and its arbitration decisions can be recovered from geometric containment (agreement 0.905 +/- 0.062 across 10 seeds, versus 0.611 +/- 0.090 for a Euclidean control). articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23575v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Low-cost tactile arrays have made touch a practical input for robot learning, but piezoresistive designs sense only pressure, while camera-based sensors that also resolve shear are too bulky to tile over a gripper. To solve this problem, we present LuxTac, a flexible, scalable optical taxel array, about 3.5 mm thick and built from off-the-shelf parts. Each taxel is a digital RGBC light-to-digital converter under a translucent white silicone layer capped by an opaque black film, so the back-scattered LED light falls monotonically with local indentation depth. The same board accepts two interchangeable gel cartridges: a plain one for normal sensing, and one with colored walls that encodes the local shear in the color of the returned light, with no camera, magnets, or bump overlay, making LuxTac, to our knowledge, the first optical taxel array to resolve shear at individual taxels. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23585v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Agricultural tasks such as harvesting and pruning require robots to reach through dense foliage, where contact is often unavoidable and vision is obstructed. Intermittent contact creates an imbalance between free-space and contact-rich observations, complicating the learning of contact-responsive behaviours. We present SPICE, a tactileconditioned diffusion policy for reaching targets in dense plant canopies using tactile sensing as the sole environmental feedback. SPICE exhibits three behaviours: moving through compliant foliage, manoeuvring around partially obstructing stems, and manipulating branches that block the target path. To the best of our knowledge, SPICE is the first tactile-conditioned diffusion policy for target reaching through physically cluttered plant canopies. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23589v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Safety certification in robotics typically rests on forward invariance of the deployed controller, a property that demands high-fidelity models at the edge of the operating envelope, exactly where models are least reliable and robots perform best. As a result, many of the behaviors we most want robots to run, from learned policies to aggressive maneuvers at the limits of traction, cannot be certified at all. We introduce recoverability, a contraction-theoretic safety concept that resolves this tension by certifying a robot's ability to reengage a trusted recovery mode rather than the invariance of a deployed behavior. We prove that switching to the recovery mode from anywhere inside a certified tube guarantees exponential convergence, even under disturbances and model error. arXiv:2611.23620v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A frozen latent world model combined with sampling-based model predictive control is a visual planner. At deployment, the executed action can depart from the commanded one, and the frozen model has no way to notice. We show that the model can be run in reverse: for any hypothesized actuation shift, it predicts what it should have observed under that shift, and comparing this prediction with what was actually observed quantifies the shift and lets the planner correct itself. Unlike the residual energy, which mixes the shift with the model's own error, the score keeps only the part of the residual that a shift can produce. This shift score detects the shift with a locally optimal test, estimates it with Cramer-Rao error bars, names the dominant generator, and compensates the planner once an alarm fires. Abstract: Noise steering improves pretrained generative robot policies by learning to select their initial noise without updating model weights. Abstract: Safe control around dynamic obstacles requires information about both distance and relative motion. Range-based filters commonly reconstruct the required range rate from successive range measurements or from obstacle-state estimators, which can introduce estimator delay or sensitivity to range noise when obstacle motion changes. We use this measurement as the derivative of an ego-centered range control barrier function (CBF) and obtain a closed-form filter on the robot's forward velocity. A measurement margin constructed from sensor error bounds accounts for errors in range, Doppler, ego velocity, and bearing. Abstract: Vision-Language-Action models have demonstrated strong manipulation capabilities. A limitation of VLA models is that most manipulation datasets focus on parallel-jaw gripper systems, making transfer to multi-finger hands challenging, particularly as teleoperation datasets are harder to collect with multi-fingered robots. arXiv:2611.23685v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A latent safety filter decides from the latent of a world model whether a planned action is safe. Conformal calibration sets the threshold of the filter so that it accepts an unsafe action only with a small probability. We call the share of safe transitions that lie in such cells the overlap. Abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have become a powerful paradigm for robotic manipulation and show strong promise for real-world deployment, making adversarial robustness critical for reliable robot operation. Abstract: Once deployed on vehicles, end-to-end driving models continuously encounter challenging scenarios, generating valuable human takeover data that capture both model outputs and human behaviors. However, human interventions are often imperfect, as drivers may intervene too late or unnecessarily. We first construct diverse trajectory candidates by augmenting the plans of the deployed model and shifting recorded human corrective maneuvers earlier in time. articles.content:

Abstract: Diffusion and flow-matching policies have become a standard choice for visuomotor imitation learning, owing to their ability to model multimodal action distributions. In memory-dependent manipulation, the robot must act on information that is no longer visible. Existing methods feed the observation history to the policy as an additional condition, while action generation still starts from Gaussian noise. However, the policy must then pick out the relevant target from a long and redundant history, leading to spurious correlations and unreliable decisions as the memory load grows. Additionally, the initial noise carries no information about what the robot has seen, leaving generation without guidance toward the remembered target. Abstract: To advance the development of embodied general navigation, zero-shot open-vocabulary multi-object navigation has attracted increasing attention, aiming to enable robots to efficiently search multiple objects in unseen environments without training. Recent methods automate this process through trajectory reflection and rule revision, enabling policy self-improvement. Consequently, the system's capacity for continued self-improvement remains constrained, even as its navigation policy evolves. articles.content:

Abstract: General robot manipulation requires both semantic competence and physical foresight. World action models (WAMs) acquire an understanding of and predictive capability over the physical world by jointly modeling visual foresight and action distributions. However, existing WAMs still lack semantic competence: they have limited ability to perform open-world scene understanding, semantic reasoning, and long-horizon planning. Although vision-language models (VLMs) provide these capabilities, effectively integrating their semantic priors into WAM prediction and control remains challenging. To address this challenge, we propose CoT-WAM, a jointly trained WAM-VLM framework. articles.content: Madras School education system (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madras_School) that was the bedrock of mass public structured education in the late 18-19th century has several similarities on how AI is trained today.They both ensures that knowledge dissemination is free.The similarities they share are as follows1) Madras school & AI distillation (Teacher-Student models) encourages Students to teach others instead of just teachers thereby reducing cost.2) Madras school & Reinforcement learning rewards or awards penalty scores based on the assessment/feedback.3) Both systems ultimately ended in rote learning and hallucinations.The other day when I noticed that several leading professors of top universities were sharing their top courses for free on YT. I immediately remembered our education system (Madras School) and how it had a profound impact in today's education system especially public mass elementary schooling system. It is also notable that today's AI training took a leaf out of it.

articles.title: Ask HN: What positive impact has AI had in the past 5 years?
articles.content:
I asked myself this question this morning and I swear I couldn't find one single thing.We still have all the problems we had before AI. AI did not solve the climate collapse, did not cure cancer, did not figure society-altering new technologies, did not make politics not suck anymore, did not solve our anxieties...If anything, we're all just more anxious today. It succeeded at making my work toxic because of the cyber warfare paranoia, I guess.AI successfully blew and continues to blow all the benchmarks it's been trained to blow. It makes long mathematical proofs nobody can read or verify about problems nobody cares about. Great?So… can someone list things that AI has genuinely improved?If there are none, why do we tolerate it?

articles.title: Show HN: Disposable – Share small AI-made tools so others can rebuild them
articles.content:
I made a site for sharing small tools made with AI.With agents, it is now quick to build a tool that fits your own task. But those tools usually get thrown away after use, and the next person who may needs something similar start again from zero. 
So I thought maybe if result or process could shared by text or code and this can lead to kind of token sharing economy.
Its name is Disposable and compared to "Open source", I named its philosophy to "Open Disposable".So the principle is "Like open source, without the upkeep. Keep the know-how, rebuild the tool your way". You can share anything you actually used and found useful, with no promise to maintain it. Others can use it as is, or give the spec that comes with it to theur own agent and have it rebuilt.If you have your own skill, prompt, or program you would like to show others, please share it. If you get stuck while sharing, let me know.Repo: https://github.com/x-ify/disposable
